# v0.49.55

This patch stops the setup and doctor commands from starting a Pi session and sending a real model request every time they run on Pi.

## Upgrading

Update the CLI (`npx @cortexkit/magic-context@latest`). The plugins are unchanged and need no restart. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Pi: `doctor` and `setup` sent a real model request on every run (issue 911, thanks @maxdai):** to list your models, the CLI ran `pi --list-models` and also `pi models list`. Pi has no `models` subcommand, so it read those two words as a prompt, opened a new session and sent it to your default model. This happened on every `doctor`, `doctor --issue` and `setup` run on Pi, and each run then waited 20 seconds for that session to time out. The CLI now runs only `pi --list-models`. Sessions left by earlier runs, named after the prompt `models list`, can be deleted from Pi's session list.

# v0.49.54

This patch makes long Pi and Oh My Pi sessions without summaries much faster to prepare each turn, and makes the emergency drop work as intended near the end of the window.

## Upgrading

Restart your host after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Pi and Oh My Pi: slow turn preparation on long sessions (issue 910, thanks @zhexulong):** on a long session without summaries, a cache of per-part token counts was smaller than the session, so every turn evicted it in the order it read it and every lookup missed. The request-size check also counted every message's tokens again on every turn. The cache is now keyed by a digest of each part's content, and the size check reuses the counts the turn already took. At 50,000 messages an appended turn went from 9.0 to 4.2 seconds, and token counts per turn from about 113,000 to 14. The requests sent to the model are unchanged.
- **The emergency drop sometimes skipped when the window was nearly full (issue 905, thanks @dhaern):** the emergency drop works out how much of the request it can't remove and drops tool results until the rest fits. It counted everything that the same pass's queued drops had already removed as content it couldn't remove, so after a large queued drop it could decide there was nothing to do. It now counts only what the request it sends still holds, on OpenCode and on Pi.
- **Pi and Oh My Pi: a background helper that failed to start ran without its tools:** Magic Context's background helpers (the summarizer, and the dreamer that maintains memories) load their tools when they start. On Oh My Pi, a startup failure (for example, storage that can't be opened) was hidden: the helper still called the model without its tools and reported success. A helper now stops before any model call when its startup fails, and the task reports the startup error, on Pi and on every supported Oh My Pi version.
- **OpenCode 2: thinking that carries only a signature was left out of size estimates (issue 905):** OpenCode 2 stores the signature of a thinking block with no visible text in a different place than OpenCode 1. Magic Context didn't find it there, so such a block counted as nothing toward the request's size. It now counts the same as on OpenCode 1.

# v0.49.53

This patch fixes Oh My Pi turns that were refused on the OpenAI Responses route and after an automatic provider retry, lets subagents on thinking models shrink again near the end of their window, and makes `ctx_search` work on the Node releases with the `node:sqlite` binding bug.

## Upgrading

Restart your host after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Oh My Pi 18.19.0: Responses turns refused with `comparison=content` (issue 909, thanks @TheOrdinaryWow):** Magic Context trimmed the whitespace around a reply that carried no tag, and Oh My Pi 18.19.0 treats any change by an extension as a rewrite: it copies the text into its own history and drops the reply's signature. The next request then no longer matched what Magic Context had planned, and was refused on every turn on that model. Replies without a tag are now left exactly as the model wrote them, a clean unsigned reply is planned the way Oh My Pi replays it, and edits Magic Context does make to older turns are applied to Oh My Pi's own history too.
- **Oh My Pi: an automatic provider retry was refused (issue 907, thanks @Zireael):** when a request failed with a rate limit, Oh My Pi's retry could arrive after the failed attempt's end notice, and Magic Context had already released the prepared request. The retry is now admitted.
- **Subagents on thinking models stayed near the end of their window (issue 905, thanks @dhaern):** after heavy reasoning, Magic Context briefly holds back changes that would invalidate the model's signed thinking. With a high threshold that hold could reach into the band where the window is nearly full, and then nothing was removed. The hold now ends where that band begins, so queued drops and the emergency drop run there.
- **`ctx_search` failed with "column index out of range" on some Node releases (issue 906, thanks @yiyi-wei):** Node 22.16 to 22.19 and 24.0 to 24.6 cannot bind numbered SQL placeholders such as `?1` by position. Every query now uses plain `?` placeholders, and a check stops numbered ones from coming back.
- **A turn whose thinking the provider rejected stayed refused:** if Anthropic rejected the thinking in the latest assistant turn, for example after a fallback put two models' thinking in one turn, every later request was rejected the same way. Magic Context now removes that turn's thinking and sends again, at most a few times.
- **A rebuild that failed late could cost a second prompt rewrite:** a pass that could not finish, or a busy store when moving OpenCode 1's compaction marker, left part of its work saved and made the next request rewrite the cached prompt again. A pass now either serves what it saved or leaves nothing behind.
- **Summary publishing sent oversized embedding requests (issue 902, thanks @iceteaSA):** a whole summary went to the embedding provider in one request. It is now split into the same bounded windows as other embeddings.

## Changed

- **`doctor --issue` warns when the OpenCode 2 plugin is outdated (issue 903):** OpenCode 2 installs a plugin once and doesn't update it on its own. The report now names the installed version beside the CLI's and says how to update. The docs have one update procedure for OpenCode 2.

## Dashboard

- **A stable token in serve mode (issue 447, thanks @yiyi-wei for pull request 897):** the dashboard can keep its access token in a file, so the address stays the same across restarts. This ships with the next dashboard build.

# v0.49.52

This patch fixes OpenCode 2 sessions that were refused on every turn with `MC-H04` once the conversation held a message without an id, and makes that refusal recover by itself when it still happens.

## Upgrading

Restart your host after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **OpenCode 2: `MC-H04` refused every turn, and `/ctx-recomp` could not clear it (issue 898, thanks @XA21X):** OpenCode 2 sends some messages without an id, such as its step-limit notice and a provider's own compaction checkpoint, and another plugin can add one too. One such message stopped Magic Context from removing the history its summaries already cover. When the conversation without that cut was larger than the model's window, the turn was refused, and every later turn with it. Magic Context now places these messages by the messages around them and makes the cut.
- **A history cut that still cannot be made no longer blocks the session:** when Magic Context cannot tell which loaded messages a summary covers and the request is over the window, it now summarizes further and tries again on the next send. If that cannot make room either, the refusal says what was wrong and what to do (`/ctx-flush` or sending again), in place of advising `/ctx-recomp`, which could not repair that state.
- **Dashboard: dismissing an already dismissed user memory changed its timestamp (issue 900, thanks @soarkit):** a repeated dismiss also told every open session that the user profile had changed. It now does nothing. The dashboard part ships with the next dashboard build.

# v0.49.51

This patch fixes Oh My Pi sessions that were refused on every turn when another extension adds its own instructions to the request, and stops `ctx_search` from repeating a call to a reranking module that is not installed.

## Upgrading

Restart your host after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Oh My Pi: every turn refused when another extension adds a message (issue 895):** on Oh My Pi 18.18.6, an extension installed from the marketplace runs after Magic Context. Superpowers 7.0.2, for example, adds its startup instructions to each request at that point. Magic Context checks every outgoing request against the one it prepared, took the extra message for conversation history it had not managed, and refused the turn (`expectedRows=3 actualRows=4`). It now accepts up to four short text messages that another extension adds, 32,768 characters in total, as long as they are not content of the session itself and do not sit inside a tool call and its result. Everything else is still refused: restored or altered session history, a changed prepared message, a broken tool pair. One case remains refused, with its own reason (`ambiguous-rewrite`): Oh My Pi rewrites a large untagged message, for example by hiding a secret in a long history summary, and another extension's message sits directly beside it.
- **Oh My Pi: sessions with an `@file` mention are checked on more providers:** such sessions used to skip the comparison of the outgoing request. They are now compared on the Anthropic, Google, Vertex, Gemini CLI, Bedrock, Ollama, OpenAI-compatible Chat and Responses routes, which were verified against Oh My Pi's own encoders. Other routes keep the earlier behaviour.
- **`ctx_search` no longer repeats a refused reranker call (issue 896):** with the Synapse reranker configured but the module absent from the machine's CortexKit daemon, every search retried the call for 30 seconds in the background, about 20 refusals per search, while the search itself had already fallen back after 1.5 seconds. The refusal is now recognized at once and remembered: for 30 seconds the first time, and for 10 minutes when the next check is refused too. A successful call clears it, so a module that was only restarting is used again within 30 seconds. Search results are the same as with reranking unavailable before; only the repeated calls are gone.
